detailed_analysis: The raw AFM height map is dominated by a large-scale tilt/bow (RMS 14.28 nm across a ~400x400 nm field), which is instrumental sample-mount tilt rather than true topography. After plane and full destripe leveling, the residual roughness collapses to Rq = 0.20 nm, indicating an atomically smooth substrate consistent with the basal plane of MoS2. The leveled residual and square-pixel panels reveal elongated, diagonally-oriented terrace domains that are brighter (raised) relative to the surrounding regions — physically these represent flat plateaus separated by discrete steps, most plausibly adsorbed peptide layers/islands or MoS2 surface terraces, not a continuously varying film. The FFT log-power spectrum shows only a diagonal streak (the terrace-edge orientation) and the horizontal scan-line artifact at f=0.0058 cyc/px (133.9 nm period, correctly excluded as instrumental), but NO discrete Fourier reflections in the targeted 3-10 nm band. The single candidate reflection was weak (1.81 sigma, below significance) and rejected. Therefore, within resolution, the MoS2-binding peptide does not form a laterally periodic (crystalline/lattice) self-assembly with a measurable repeat spacing in this region; instead it decorates the surface as flat-topped islands/terraces. The sub-Angstrom-to-Angstrom residual corrugation (~0.2 nm RMS) is consistent with a monolayer-thin, conformal adsorbate rather than a bulky ordered lattice.

scientific_claims.claim: The MoS2-binding peptide layer on MoS2 exhibits no resolvable lateral periodicity in the 3-10 nm band (candidate reflection only 1.8 sigma, below significance), forming flat-topped terrace/island domains on an atomically smooth substrate (post-leveling Rq = 0.20 nm) rather than an ordered periodic self-assembly.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Distinguishes island/terrace-mediated adsorption from crystalline 2D self-assembly, informing whether this peptide templates ordered structures on 2D materials — relevant for biomolecule-directed nanofabrication and biosensing interfaces.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed that MoS2-binding peptides adsorb as flat non-periodic terrace domains rather than forming laterally ordered self-assembled lattices on MoS2 basal planes?

analysis_approach: Load the prior leveled height array (physical nm) and quantify the terrace/step structure — segment discrete height levels and measure step heights across the diagonal edges to identify layer thickness (e.g. MoS2 monolayer steps ~0.6 nm).
